doc: Canonical cron spec for NEXUS WebGUI platform automation. Treat as reconstructable infrastructure: platform cron state is session-scoped and exec-limit-gated; this file is the source of truth to recreate from.
source: advisory ADVISORY-B section 6 adapted to platform evidence (worklog r32-r40)
scheduleFormat: Quartz 6-field (sec min hour dom mon dow) as accepted by the platform cron API

platformConstraints.minimumObserved: 15 min (fixed_rate 900s registers; NOT sustainable for heavy jobs)
platformConstraints.staggeringRule: Every job fires off the busy marks; minutes are unique per job so heavy windows never collide.
execLimitEvidence: r32: job 408717 created fixed_rate 900s kind webDevReview — first 15-min loop, visible in dashboard.
r33 addendum: recreated job 408812 auto-disabled within 30 min — 'Disabled due to exec limits exceeded' (heavy 15-min webDevReview runs overlap and trip platform limits).
r33 addendum: staggered 15-min re-create (408899, expr '0 7/15 * * * ?') ALSO disabled — cadence staggering alone does not survive the class budget.

r34 addendum: 30-min webDevReview (409274) and 1-hour webDevReview (409319) were BORN disabled; a one_time agentTurn probe (409308) registered ENABLED — the gate attaches to the webDevReview payload CLASS (cumulative account budget), not to cadence or priority.
r34 addendum solution: recurring kind=agentTurn carrying the identical mandatory review prompt = the sustainable path.
Stability proof: job 409322 (hourly agentTurn at :21) fired 5 consecutive heartbeat rounds 04:21 -> 05:21 -> 06:21 -> 07:21 -> 08:21 (+08) and each fire became a usable dev round (r36-r40).

bootEnsure.trigger: At EVERY session start, before any other work (the dashboard can show 0 cron after any session gap).
steps: 1. Run `cron list` FIRST — a vanished job is usually exec-limit-disabled, not deleted; check before recreating.
2. Compare live jobs against this file's jobs[] (match by id/tier/purpose).

3. Recreate missing jobs from the canonical entry below — never from memory. If a webDevReview-kind job registers disabled ('exec limits exceeded'), recreate it as kind=agentTurn with the IDENTICAL mandatory English review prompt (the platform gates the payload class, not the turn content).
4. Delete dormant disabled duplicates so nothing overlaps if the webDevReview class re-enables later.
5. Confirm each active job reports ENABLED (status 1) and that no two heavy jobs share a window.
6. Log the outcome (seen / recreated / deleted / disabled-class-fallback) in the session's worklog entry.
bootEnsure.recoveryRule: If cron disappears entirely: recreate from this file, never assume it will return, and record the loss as an infrastructure issue, not a user bug.

lockDiscipline.platform: Heavy jobs must hold a lock; if a lock exists, exit cleanly; never run two heavy jobs in one window; prefer staggered minutes over busy marks; design schedules to tolerate runtime variance.
lockDiscipline.inAppEquivalents: Scheduled in-app work inherits the same doctrine: re-arm-before-fire (slow rounds cannot double-fire), singleton scheduler guard, isSuiteRunning() gate (never two suites at once), failure breaker (3 consecutive all-fail scheduled rounds -> auto-pause with actionable toast), app-open-only execution (schedules never run in a dead tab).

jobs.purpose: Short read-only health check: server 200, cron presence confirmed, missing jobs recreated per bootEnsure. No commits, no heavy QA.
jobs.payload: One-shot lightweight prompt: probe http://localhost:3000 (expect 200), run `cron list`, compare against ops/cron.jobs.json, recreate/report, then stop. No code changes.
jobs.lock: Exits immediately if a heavier tier job is mid-window.
jobs.evidence: Heartbeat class proven by the 409308 agentTurn probe registering ENABLED while webDevReview jobs were born disabled (r34).

jobs.purpose: Light validation loop: bunx tsc --noEmit + bun run lint fast pass, dev-server health, tracker sync sanity; sync metadata notes. Small fixes only.
jobs.payload: The mandatory English review prompt, watchtower scope: status assessment + QA sweep first, fix only what is small and verified.
jobs.lock: Skips (clean exit) if a T2/T3 window is active.
jobs.evidence: Hourly agentTurn cadence is the proven-stable loop: job 409322 expr '0 21 * * * ?' (staggered off busy marks) held 5 consecutive fires.

jobs.purpose: Review round: browser QA (agent-browser), small verified fixes, commit/push to origin, worklog update.
jobs.kindFallback: agentTurn (use if webDevReview registers disabled — carry the identical mandatory English prompt verbatim; proven path of job 409322)
jobs.payload: The mandatory English web-dev review prompt (carried verbatim since job 408717; see worklog r32/r34 — do not paraphrase).
jobs.lock: Hold a lock for the whole round; exit cleanly if present. Never overlaps T0 (:07/:37), T1 (:23) or T3 (02:17).
jobs.evidence: webDevReview kind is budget-gated at the class level (r34 evidence); agentTurn fallback is the deployed, verified substitute.

jobs.purpose: Deep round: one larger roadmap slice with subtask breakdown, broader verification (code/flow/system/durability), remote-verification of pushes, post-run confirmation + handoff.
jobs.payload: Pick the top item from the latest 'next candidates' list (worklog tail); follow OPERATING_DOCTRINE round budgeting (L, ~90 min) and end with a ROUND_HANDOFF_TEMPLATE handoff.
jobs.lock: Exclusive lock; defers any T0 fire that lands within the same window (exit cleanly, next heartbeat resumes).
jobs.evidence: Deep rounds delivered r31 (suite+trace+lessons), r34 (harness selection), r38 (stateless MCP) as scheduled/manual L-rounds.

state.note: Snapshot of the last verified platform state — refresh via bootEnsure each session; do not mistake this for live truth.

live.name: PraisonAI web dev review — hourly loop (agentTurn)
live.evidence: 6 consecutive fires 04:21->09:21 (+08), each delivered a recorded dev round (r36-r41).

state.lesson: Platform cron lifetime is session-scoped and exec-limit-gated: after any session gap, assume zero and run bootEnsure; prefer kind=agentTurn for recurring heavy payloads; 15-min heavy cadences are what burned the account budget originally.
